title: The shipped deployment grants Editor (write) to any unassigned authenticated key and leaves broad read surfaces public
evidence: The code is fail-closed — `public_reads_enabled()` ends `.unwrap_or(false)` (rbac_gate.rs:126-133) and main.rs:807-813 refuses to start owner-less unless `RBAC_ALLOW_OWNERLESS` is set — but docker-compose.unified.yml:111-112 sets `RBAC_PUBLIC_READS=1` and `RBAC_ALLOW_OWNERLESS=1` (with `:-1` defaults), so an unassigned pubkey resolves to Editor (role_store.rs:359-366, rbac.rs:68-70). Independently of that toggle, the `/analytics` scope leaves every GET public as "harmless operational telemetry" (analytics/mod.rs:169-170), and the `/api/ontology` scope gates only mutations — "POST PUT DELETE gated, all GET public" (ontology/mod.rs:1645), including `GET /ontology/provenance` and `/ontology/reports`; class-count is "unauthenticated by design" (ontology_class_count_handler.rs:25).
failure: First boot of the shipped compose: anyone with any nostr key gets Editor (graph/settings mutation); anyone at all reads ontology content, provenance reports, GPU/ops telemetry.
marked_by_authors: yes — CORRECTED ADR-2070 note and DIVERGENCE in VC-33.6; recorded as ADR-2027's deliberate demo default that "stays".

title: An explicit `public: false` is overridden by any owl-class marker: the publish gate is an OR
evidence: `is_kg_included` returns true when public true OR owl_class Some (vault/mod.rs:162-163). The ADR-2070 closeout itself records: "an explicit public false plus a class marker remains included by policy - is_kg_included is an OR, so a valid owl-class overrides public false (vault/mod.rs:162-163)".
failure: An author marks a sensitive vault page `public: false`; a tool-inserted or stale `owl-class` key publishes it into GRAPH_KNOWLEDGE, where it is served on public GET endpoints (see F-01). Silent, and by policy.
marked_by_authors: yes (DIVERGENCE, VC-21.12) — but as recorded policy, not as a tracked defect.

title: Erasure cannot be satisfied end-to-end: Pod delete leaves RuVector embeddings searchable, and the append-only provenance graph has no shredding decision
evidence: `deleteAgentMemory` never calls any RuVector delete — "embedding row persists and stays searchable" (docs/DATA-authority-erasure.md:87; agentMemory.ts:191-198), and a second direct read-only RuVector client now exists (Cargo.toml:133-138, marked DRIFT). Provenance is append-only — "no DELETE, DROP or CLEAR" (provenance_emitter.rs:32-33) — and the erasure-vs-provenance choice (crypto-shredding vs out-of-scope) is only PROPOSED (ADR-2102).
failure: A deletion request removes the Pod document but the vector row stays semantically queryable and the actor's DID/attribution persists forever in GRAPH_PROVENANCE; an erasure or audit demand cannot be met from this system.
marked_by_authors: yes (DIVERGENCE for RuVector; PROPOSED ADR-2102 for provenance) — but the combined erasure failure is not tracked as one item.

title: A force-full sync destroys governed writes made directly to the assert graph
evidence: On `FORCE_FULL_SYNC`, `rebuild_assert_graph` does CLEAR GRAPH assert then INSERT (github_sync_service.rs:1004); the diagram notes "this CLEAR wipes the ENTIRE assert graph including runtime OWL classes/axioms added via the governed write door (github_sync_service.rs:930-932)" and "a class added via add_owl_class/add_axiom between full-syncs is NOT itself in GRAPH_PROVENANCE-protected history for the assert graph - only re-derivation from the corpus ... restores it". `rematerialise_decisions` restores DecisionRecord quads only, "non-fatal on failure" (github_sync_service.rs:1020-1026, :1082).
failure: Operator sets FORCE_FULL_SYNC=1 to rebuild the projection; every class/axiom accepted through the governed write door (power-user POST /ontology/classes, /ontology/axioms) vanishes with no warning and no restore path unless it also exists as a corpus page; failed decision re-materialisation is logged and dropped.
marked_by_authors: no — stated in diagram notes as a known consequence, with no Debt/Drift/Open marker and no tracked remedy.

title: The append-only provenance/ontology store has no point-in-time backup and cannot be re-derived, while the authority docs still disagree with the code about primacy
evidence: backup-sqlite.sh covers the four SQLite DBs only; "Oxigraph still has NO point-in-time backup - that bullet stands" (VC-22.11 DriftNote); PROPOSED ADR-2103 would add it as a REQUIRED member — implementation none. GRAPH_PROVENANCE is "restore-only because it cannot be re-derived" (VC-22.7). Separately: "legacy ADRs assign primacy to Oxigraph 132 / Pod 050-052 / GitHub 051 ... code resolves as this matrix, legacy prose not reconciled" (DATA-authority-erasure.md:97).
failure: Disk loss on the Oxigraph volume permanently destroys the signed audit trail (and the knowledge/agent graphs). An operator following the unreconciled legacy ADRs may attempt an Oxigraph-first restore — which, since the corpus is the write-master, resurrects erased or superseded content.
confidence: high on the backup absence; medium and inferred on the resurrection scenario.
marked_by_authors: yes (PROPOSED ADR-2103; DIVERGENCE for the authority prose) — open with no owner or date.

title: One signing secret authenticates the bead publisher, the forum bridge and three ACSP panel identities, and the bridge re-signs everything under its own key
evidence: "bridge bot keypair VISIONCLAW_NOSTR_PRIVKEY shared by both publisher and bridge" (nostr_bead_publisher.rs:18, nostr_bridge.rs:12); "three separate relay connections under three different panel identities can exist concurrently, all using the same bridge secret" (VC-24.11); the bridge "re-sign(s) under bridge keypair, preserve source_event tag" with "NIP-26 delegation not wired, service-signing only" (nostr_bridge.rs:29,65,169).
failure: Compromise of any context that loads this one env var forges kind-31402 ActionRequests, bead provenance events and forum republishes; the relay-side "registered pubkeys" gate then protects the attacker's use of an already-registered key. Structurally, every forum event already displays as the bridge, so per-agent accountability on the governance forum is absent.
confidence: high on sharing/re-signing (stated); medium and inferred on forgery impact via the relay registration model.
marked_by_authors: partially — NIP-26 divergence is marked (VC-24.8); the single-secret blast radius is stated in VC-24.11 but not marked as a risk.

title: The material contradicts itself on whether a restart can drop a signed human decision (ElevationActor boot reconciliation)
evidence: VC-24.4 (ADR-2110): "pending is no longer only in memory. A Reconcile at boot reloads durable pending rows ... so a kind-31403 arriving after a restart no longer hits an empty map and drops the human's signed decision (elevation_actor.rs:1009, :1330, :1340)". VC-24.5 (ADR-2101), in the same file at the same verified_commit af3dff3f: "STILL OPEN on this path: the ElevationActor poll ... has no boot reconciliation, so a case lost between publish and persist is not reloaded on restart. ADR-2101 adds that to DecisionElevationActor only".
failure: If VC-24.5 is current, a restart between a PR-terminal publish and `set_status` permanently loses the terminal status — the case never leaves `elevating` and the human's decision is unrecorded in the store. If VC-24.4 is current, VC-24.5's "STILL OPEN" misdirects whoever triages it. One note is stale and unverified at the stamped commit either way.
confidence: high that the contradiction exists; low-medium on which side is true (requires reading elevation_actor.rs at af3dff3f).
marked_by_authors: no — neither note flags the conflict with the other.

title: Feature flags are process-global, shared by every user, replaced wholesale, unpersisted — and the only real gate among them is flippable by any authenticated mutator
evidence: FEATURE_FLAGS is a static Lazy Arc Mutex (state.rs:15); update does `*flags = request.into_inner()` — "WHOLESALE REPLACE - no field merge, a partial POST silently resets omitted flags" (feature_flags_handlers.rs:28-29); "ontology_validation is the ONLY flag read as a real GATE - it short-circuits ontology validation with an ErrorResponse" (ontology/mod.rs:332-335); the POST sits behind only the scope's mutations_only wrap (analytics/mod.rs:170, :204) plus an AuthenticatedUser extractor; flags reset on restart. OPEN ADR-2059 lists global/shared/unpersisted/wholesale as open.
failure: Any authenticated user (Editor under F-01) POSTs `{"ontology_validation": false}` — validation is disabled for every user and every request process-wide; a partial POST simultaneously resets the other flag; a restart silently restores defaults, so post-incident flag state explains nothing.
marked_by_authors: yes (OPEN ADR-2059) — but the "any authenticated user can disable the only validation gate" consequence is not drawn.

title: Governance KPIs are computed from unverified, self-asserted actor DIDs
evidence: "ProvenanceStatus::Attributed means a well-formed pubkey was asserted, NOT that a signature was verified - the wire carries no sig field (provenance.rs:29-38)". Those events persist to kpi_agent_events with the declared intent verbatim (migrations/sqlite/0006; sqlite_kpi_repository.rs:245) and feed Trust Variance, HITL Precision and augmentation ratio (kpi_compute.rs:98, :140, :213).
failure: A misbehaving agent attributes its actions to a human's DID (a 64-hex check is the only barrier); Trust Variance and HITL Precision — the controls meant to detect exactly this — are polluted, and the whelk-gate exclusion (kpi_compute.rs:140) does nothing against spoofed human attribution.
confidence: high that no signature exists; medium and inferred that decisions are made on these numbers.
marked_by_authors: yes (SECURITY note in VC-27.13) — but its propagation into KPI integrity is not traced.

title: Post-sync Whelk reasoning has no timeout and no axiom cap, and the same engine gates elevation approvals
evidence: "module doc claims complete EL reasoning (whelk_inference_engine.rs:5) but infer() lines 412-467 has no tokio timeout or axiom-count cap"; `approve_with_gate` runs `WhelkInferenceEngine.check_axiom_set` on the elevation decision path (elevation_actor.rs:1260); the sync cycle including reasoning runs from a boot task (app_state.rs:614) and after every sync; the checksum cache only helps when the ontology is unchanged.
failure: One large or adversarial ontology after a corpus change makes `run_post_sync_reasoning` consume unbounded CPU — the boot sync stalls, and elevation approvals block inside the gate with no circuit breaker.
confidence: medium-high (absence of bounds is stated; hang duration inferred).
marked_by_authors: yes (DOC-DRIFT) — but as doc drift, not as an availability defect.

title: Decision fan-out is dual-write with no reconciliation: durable in SQLite, best-effort in Oxigraph, and signed attribution is never re-materialised
evidence: "no cross-store 2PC - the durable decision commits in SQLite first ... the Oxigraph write is best-effort, writeback_committed flips only on Ok (enrichment_proposals_handler.rs:556, :574)" — and nothing in the material reconciles `writeback_triggered=true / committed=false` rows later. After full sync, "attribution is deliberately NOT re-materialised here - the signed PROV-O attribution stays in GRAPH_PROVENANCE (github_sync_service.rs:1032-1041)" — the same graph with no backup (F-05).
failure: An Oxigraph hiccup at decision time leaves the KG permanently missing a summary the durable record says was triggered (no retry path shown); after any full sync, assert-graph decision records carry no attribution, so the signed chain is only as durable as the unbacked provenance graph.
confidence: medium-high (no-reconciliation is absence of evidence in the material).
marked_by_authors: partially — "no cross-store 2PC" is noted in VC-22.8; the missing reconciliation and the attribution gap are stated as design without a marker.

title: The human-rationale gate reads the risk tier the proposing agent declared, and first-contact cases carry no tier at all
evidence: "the gate reads the tier RECORDED ON THE CASE, which today is the proposing agent's DECLARED risk_tier ... a case with no row yet carries no tier, so first-contact bridge decisions are ungated (handlers/enrichment_proposals_handler.rs:332, :393)". The mirrored client-side constant is explicitly "a courtesy, not the rule" (brokerCaseQueue.ts:186).
failure: An agent labels a high-impact mutation tier low — or has the bridge decide before the case row exists — and the 20-character rationale requirement (ADR-2110 FR2.2, the HITL control) never triggers; the decision is recorded and write-back eligible.

title: Every ontology HTTP handler is one refactor away from a runtime panic: sync-over-async CQRS behind a load-bearing blocking wrapper
evidence: "the CQRS query handlers are sync-over-async - they enter a nested block_on. Called inline on an actix worker they panic with 'Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime' and drop the connection (ontology_handler.rs:436-439)". The last two bare calls were closed only on 2026-09-16 (ad8b83ad4); "DEBT: the wrapping is load-bearing only while the CQRS handlers stay sync - the test module says to delete it if they become async-direct (ontology_handler.rs:1107)".
failure: A new endpoint added without the wrapper — or a well-meaning refactor to async-direct that deletes the wrapper per the test note — reintroduces the panic on the worker thread; under load this presents as dropped connections across the whole ontology surface. The defect has historically regrown at least three times.
confidence: high on the mechanism; medium on recurrence.
marked_by_authors: yes (DEBT note) — but as a maintenance caveat, not an availability risk.

title: Authentication state is per-process: NIP-98 replay cache and Nostr sessions live in memory; Redis persistence is optional and unverified
evidence: REPLAY_CACHE is an in-process "Mutex<HashMap>" (nip98.rs:215) with a 60 s token window (TOKEN_MAX_AGE_SECONDS, nip98.rs:169,362); NostrService sessions are an in-memory users map unless the redis feature AND REDIS_URL are set (nostr_service.rs:151, :164), and the Redis scope note reads "Not enabled by default; deployment not verified — ADR-2004 all-non-triple-state wording needs scope".
failure: A restart wipes the replay cache — a token intercepted within its window can be replayed once across the restart — and drops every bearer-authenticated session (including WS header-token clients, VC-32.1) until re-auth. Running two instances behind a balancer breaks replay protection and session validity entirely (inferred: the material never shows a multi-instance deployment).
confidence: medium (in-memory nature is stated; restart-replay and multi-instance consequences are inferred).
marked_by_authors: partially — the Redis session scope is marked in VC-22.1; the replay cache's process locality is not flagged anywhere.

title: Governance and ops entry points that silently do nothing: TriggerReasoning forwards to an actor that no longer exists, flanked by a dead pipeline path and log-only opcodes
evidence: OntologyActor's TriggerReasoning handler "forwards to ReasoningActor per comment lines 918-920 which no longer exists" (ontology_actor.rs:904-920 note) — the message is accepted and routed nowhere, with no error to the sender. Adjacent: `on_ontology_modified`/`trigger_reasoning` has "no caller ... outside tests/integration/pipeline_test.rs:94" while its doc comment claims GitHubSyncService calls it (VC-20.3, marked Drift/Debt); `/multi-mcp` request_agents, request_performance and request_topology handlers "only log at debug" (multi_mcp_websocket_handler.rs:664-705, marked DEBT).
failure: During an incident, an operator "triggers reasoning" or requests agents/performance/topology and receives success-shaped silence; time is lost to controls wired to nothing, and the TriggerReasoning no-op is invisible because nothing errors.
confidence: high on the forwarding note; medium that real senders exist in practice.
marked_by_authors: no for the TriggerReasoning dead forward; yes (Drift/Debt and DEBT) for the two adjacent items.

title: Erasure is a Pod-only delete: embeddings stay live and searchable in RuVector, with a second server-side reader added on top
evidence: "DIVERGENCE: no reverse tombstone to RuVector - embedding row persists and stays searchable (docs/DATA-authority-erasure.md:87)" (VC-22.6); "this Pod-side delete never calls mcp__claude-flow__memory_delete or any RuVector endpoint - RuVector is external Postgres reached only via MCP, no delete-propagation hook exists in this path" (VC-22.6); `deleteResource` treats 404 as success — "already-absent is not an error" (client/src/services/solidPod/ldpClient.ts:210,215), so the UI reports a completed delete even when the resource was never there; "DRIFT: the server now also holds a direct read-only RuVector client (tokio-postgres from RUVECTOR_PG_CONNINFO, crate visionclaw-memory-cloud), so MCP-only access holds for writes and deletes but no longer for reads, and the embedding row this path leaves behind has a second consumer Cargo.toml:133-138"; the erasure design for provenance is likewise unresolved — crypto-shredding is only "PROPOSED ADR-2102", and retraction "only ADDS dl:validTo and deletes nothing - history never removed (provenance_writer.rs:218,478-502)"; the RuVector-side fix is punted to "agentbox ADR-2060 … referenced, not superseded" (VC-22.10 note).
failure: A subject (or the client's DPO) requests erasure of agent memory → the UI calls `deleteAgentMemory` → the Pod JSON-LD resource is DELETEd (or already absent, still reported as success) → the operator records erasure complete → no call ever reaches RuVector: the delete path "never calls mcp__claude-flow__memory_delete or any RuVector endpoint" → the embedding row persists in external Postgres → since the server now holds a direct read-only RuVector client, the erased content is retrievable by two consumers, not one → an audit or the subject's own query finds the "deleted" memory via semantic search → the client leaves.

title: Oxigraph holds non-re-derivable data (the signed provenance ledger, runtime-added ontology, observed graph) and has no backup of any kind
evidence: "Oxigraph still has NO point-in-time backup - that bullet stands" (VC-22.11 DriftNote, after RESOLVED ADR-2069); REQUIRED_DBS is settings/enrichment/kpi only (scripts/backup-sqlite.sh:75) while the script's completeness contract refuses only missing *members* (:242-245) — so a green backup run certifies a set that never contained the only unrecoverable store; "PROPOSED ADR-2103: Oxigraph gains a point-in-time snapshot as a REQUIRED backup member… GRAPH_PROVENANCE is restore-only because it cannot be re-derived" — proposed, not implemented; VC-22.1 names GRAPH_PROVENANCE as the write-master for "Event journal / provenance", so its loss loses the journal itself.
failure: Oxigraph storage is lost (volume failure, host rebuild, accidental `CLEAR`) → the operator restores from the documented backup set → backup-sqlite.sh restores settings/enrichment/kpi and publishes a verified MANIFEST — Oxigraph is not a member of the set at all → GRAPH_KNOWLEDGE and the assert graph are largely re-derived from the corpus → GRAPH_PROVENANCE cannot be re-derived by design: it is append-only ("no DELETE, DROP or CLEAR issued against this graph", provenance_emitter.rs:32-33, verified by the append_only test at :908) and full-sync rematerialisation deliberately does not reproduce attribution — "the signed PROV-O attribution stays in GRAPH_PROVENANCE… the corpus decision page carries only the summary" (github_sync_service.rs:1032-1041) → the operator cannot produce the signed audit trail for enrichment decisions and elevation approvals the client contracted for → separate but compounding: any class added through the governed write door was already wiped by the same rebuild path ("this CLEAR wipes the ENTIRE assert graph including runtime OWL classes/axioms added via the governed write door", github_sync_service.rs:930-932; "a class added via add_owl_class/add_axiom between full-syncs is NOT itself in GRAPH_PROVENANCE-protected history") and decision rematerialisation is "non-fatal on failure" (github_sync_service.rs:1082, 1020-1026).

title: Shipped deployment posture: public anonymous reads, no Owner, and any freshly generated Nostr key resolves to Editor — with private-intended pages leaking through the owl-class OR-gate
evidence: "RBAC_PUBLIC_READS is fail-closed in code - .unwrap_or(false) (rbac_gate.rs:126-133) - and set on only by compose (docker-compose.unified.yml:111)"; "The shipped compose inverts both (docker-compose.unified.yml:111, :112, with the :-1 default), so an unassigned pubkey resolves to Editor (role_store.rs:359). The open posture is ADR-2027's deliberate demo default and stays"; main.rs:807,813 refuses owner-less startup *only* when the flag is unset — the compose sets it; the OR-gate divergence is recorded at closeout (VC-21.12, "DIVERGENCE"); the client-side gating divergence (VC-33.6, "DIVERGENCE… this is the ENTIRE client-side gating surface — a binary power-user flag"); note the compose citations have drifted (VC-33.6 DOC-DRIFT: the block moved to :106/:107 via ADR-2108 then ADR-2114 and was never re-anchored) — the posture itself is unchanged.
failure: The operator deploys with the shipped compose → `RBAC_PUBLIC_READS=1` and `RBAC_ALLOW_OWNERLESS=1` are set, inverting the code's fail-closed defaults → any anonymous GET on a safe method passes through with no auth ("200 passthrough", rbac_gate.rs:248-253) → simultaneously, any user who generates a keypair and authenticates hits `effective_role` with no assignment and resolves to default_role **Editor** (role_store.rs:359, 366) under a server with no Owner at all → private material reaches those public reads through the inclusion gate: `is_kg_included` is an OR, so "an explicit public false plus a class marker remains included by policy… a valid owl-class overrides public false" (vault/mod.rs:162-163) — a page its author marked private but which carries an `owl-class` frontmatter marker is ingested into GRAPH_KNOWLEDGE and served anonymously → unassigned-Editor strangers also clear the RBAC gate on mutating routes; the client's UI gating is a single binary `isPowerUser` flag that "never [fetches] its own resolved role", so nothing warns the operator before the server rejects (or fails to reject) writes.
confidence: high (both behaviours are stated facts; the exposure chain composes them directly).

title: All credentials sit in a plaintext `.env`; the SOPS rollout was proposed and never executed
evidence: "Credentials → .env plaintext filesystem"; "PROPOSED ADR-2104: execute the SOPS rollout or formally withdraw ADR-109 - plaintext .env is documented as the interim state either way; a 43MB scripts/sops binary dated 2026-05-09 is present and gitignored, but no .sops.yaml, secrets.enc.yaml or sops-env.sh exists (docs/DATA-authority-erasure.md:112)". The same file holds VISIONCLAW_AGENT_KEY, VISIONCLAW_NOSTR_PRIVKEY (F-13), PRIVATE_REPO_GITHUB_PAT (VC-28.6).

marked_by_authors: yes (PROPOSED ADR-2104 / divergence node in VC-22.1).

evidence: append-only is an invariant with a test (provenance_emitter.rs:32-33, :908); "Retraction only ADDS dl:validTo and deletes nothing - history never removed (provenance_writer.rs:218,478-502)"; ADR-2102 (crypto-shred or scope-out) is proposed only.
